The Z-transform \(X(z)\) of a discrete-time signal \(x[n]\) is defined by the power series
\[

\]
which converges only inside a region of the complex plane called the region of convergence (ROC). The DTFT of \(x[n]\) is obtained simply by restricting the same series to the unit circle \(z=e^{j\omega}\). Consequently, a necessary condition for the DTFT to exist (in the ordinary sense) is that the unit circle must lie inside the ROC of \(X(z)\). This immediately shows that statement (C) is true.

Thus the true statements are (C) and (D).

\]
